title: AI brief for South African business, 11 July 2026
summary: Google Search upgrades to Gemini 3.5 Flash globally, making AI agents more accessible. Chinese models now account for 30-46% of US enterprise token usage due to cost advantages. The UN's AI for Good Summit focuses on global AI standards.

items.headline: Google Search upgrades to Gemini 3.5 Flash globally
items.what: Google announced at I/O 2026 that it is upgrading Search with Gemini 3.5 Flash as the default model in AI Mode globally. This includes a reimagined AI-powered Search box.
items.soWhat: South African businesses can now access more advanced AI capabilities directly through Google Search, which may improve local search results and AI-assisted queries. No additional cost for users.
items.relatedTitle: ChatGPT vs Gemini vs Perplexity for a South African business

items.headline: Chinese AI models now 30-46% of US enterprise token usage
items.what: CNBC investigation confirmed Chinese AI models account for 30-46% of enterprise API token usage in US developer platforms, up from 11% average in prior 12 months, due to being 60-90% cheaper than Western models.
items.soWhat: South African businesses using AI APIs should evaluate cost-performance tradeoffs of Chinese models like DeepSeek and Z.ai, which may offer significant savings for non-critical tasks.
items.relatedTitle: The best AI tools for a South African small business (2026)

items.headline: UN AI for Good Summit focuses on global AI standards
items.what: The UN's AI for Good Summit running 7-10 July in Geneva brings together stakeholders to develop AI standards and policies for innovation and digital transformation worldwide.
items.soWhat: South African businesses should monitor outcomes as these global standards may influence future local AI regulations and compliance requirements under POPIA.
items.relatedTitle: POPIA-compliant AI tools for South African business

items.headline: US executive order prioritizes AI innovation and security
items.what: US Presidential Executive Order 14409 directs agencies to modernize systems for AI while prioritizing cybersecurity of critical infrastructure and national security systems.
items.soWhat: While focused on US systems, this may lead to more secure AI tools becoming available globally that South African businesses could benefit from, particularly for cybersecurity.

items.headline: DeepSeek's open-weight frontier AI model challenges closed models
items.what: DeepSeek's January 2025 release of its R1 reasoning LLM demonstrated Chinese capability to produce frontier models at lower cost, intensifying debate about open vs closed model ecosystems.
items.soWhat: South African developers can access DeepSeek's open weights for local experimentation, but most businesses will continue using commercial APIs due to infrastructure requirements.
items.relatedTitle: The AI benchmarks, explained for a normal person

items.headline: Enterprise AI agents shift to outcome-based pricing
items.what: Major vendors like Zendesk and HubSpot have moved from per-user/month pricing to outcome-based models (e.g. $0.50-$1.50 per automated resolution) for AI agents in 2026.
items.soWhat: South African businesses implementing AI customer service can now align costs directly with business outcomes rather than fixed fees, improving ROI calculations.
items.relatedTitle: AI customer service on WhatsApp for South African business
